To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have cloned and expressed the ovine p35, p40 subunits and the ovine IL- 12 heterodimer.
ovine IL12 has biological activity, and this activity can be detected in ovine and human cells.
we have cloned the coding sequences for ovine p35/p40 subunits of IL-12, expressed the subunits in CHO cells and demonstrated that the heterodimer is secreted and has biological activity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the isolation and characterization of ovine IL12 and its biological activities.
the development of ovine IL12 as a vaccine adjuvant.
the development of an ovine IL-2/IL-12 system for the study of sheep immune function and the development of a potential ovine model for human immune disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ovine IL12 is similar to the human IL12 in terms of structure and function.
ovine IL12 has a similar biological activity as human IL-12.
the biological properties of ovine IL12 are similar to its human equivalent.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ovine p35/p40 cDNA can be used to generate biologically active IL-12, which can stimulate proliferation of ovine and human PBMNC.
the ovine IL-2 gene is expressed in ovine PBMCs, the protein is secreted from CHO cells, and the ovine IL12 p35/p40 heterodimer is biologically active on ovine and hu PBMCs.
ovine IL12 has biological activity and can be used to study the effects of IL12 in ovine species.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ovine IL12 can be used in a variety of in vitro assays to study the immune system of sheep.
ovine IL12 is a functional cytokine that is capable of stimulating the proliferation of ovine PBMNCs.
the IL-12 p70 heterodimer is a potent activator of T lymphocytes and NK cells, and is an important mediator of the innate and adaptive immune responses.
